verdict.root_cause: A scheduled platform-automation fault-injection routine attached a traffic-shaping container to cartservice's network namespace at 12:20:04, imposing a fixed 300ms egress delay with no jitter, and unlike every earlier attachment in the window this one was never paired with a removal, so it was still in force at the 12:23:30 alerts [tr_1a6b4ecd47ad]. Every cart call therefore pays a synthetic delay, propagating up the checkout path: checkoutservice's error ratio steps ~125x above baseline while still serving most requests [tr_091795de4d3f], and both cartservice and checkoutservice logs show per-step gaps growing from milliseconds to about a second with no error, timeout or startup text [tr_eb7e3f4ea605, tr_40505355587d]. The mechanism is waiting on a slowed dependency, not a broken artifact or a wrong value in cart's own config.
verdict.reasoning: The only change outstanding at onset is the unpaired traffic-shaping attachment, ~3 minutes before alerts; the hotfix image and REDIS_ADDR edits from the same chaos triplet were both reverted beforehand [tr_1a6b4ecd47ad]. Symptoms match injected delay rather than failure: cartservice logs routine cart operations to within seconds of window end with no errors, startup banners, image-pull or redis messages [tr_eb7e3f4ea605]; checkoutservice peaks well below total failure, returns to zero intermittently, and steps discretely rather than ramping, arguing against internal exhaustion [tr_091795de4d3f], while its tail shows orders completing with successful payments and monotonic offsets [tr_40505355587d]. Both services show timing inflation to roughly a second per step [tr_eb7e3f4ea605, tr_40505355587d]. Latency downstream with errors surfacing only as deadline spillover at the caller is dependency_latency; cartservice is blamed because the delay is applied at its interface and checkout/frontend/loadgenerator symptoms follow by call order. cartservice's own error series is absent in both incident and baseline windows, so it neither supports nor contradicts this [tr_d9521161aa64]. The fix is detaching the injected shaping, not rolling back an artifact.
open_questions: checkoutservice's change point is 12:02:30, ~18 minutes before the shaping attach at 12:20:04, so the shaping cannot explain the earlier elevation — possibly a separate earlier injection or a change-point artifact [tr_091795de4d3f, tr_1a6b4ecd47ad].
No latency metric was queried for either service; the 300ms figure comes from the change record and is corroborated only by log timestamp gaps, a weak proxy [tr_eb7e3f4ea605, tr_40505355587d].

Both log queries were truncated across the entire 12:02-12:23 interval, so onset behaviour and any peer-named error were never observed, and checkout's metric has no peer dimension to confirm the failing calls are cart calls [tr_40505355587d, tr_091795de4d3f].

alternatives.root_cause: An earlier chaos step around 12:02 (the hotfix image push/revert cycle) degraded the checkout path, and the shaping attach is coincidental to the alert time.
alternatives.why_not: The hotfix reference was already reverted ~14 minutes before onset and cartservice shows no startup or image-pull failures, so no wrong artifact was running at onset [tr_1a6b4ecd47ad, tr_eb7e3f4ea605].
alternatives.note: It does align better with the 12:02:30 change point, which keeps it plausible.

alternatives.root_cause: checkoutservice itself degraded — an internal fault or an unexamined dependency such as payment, shipping or productcatalog — and cart's slowness is incidental.
alternatives.why_not: Checkout's baseline was flat and clean, its errors step rather than ramp, and payment and publish paths were observed succeeding; no checkout-side change is recorded, whereas an unreverted delay sits on its cart dependency [tr_091795de4d3f, tr_40505355587d, tr_1a6b4ecd47ad].

proposal.expected_effect: Nothing changes; no action proposed. The fix the evidence implies — detaching the unpaired traffic-shaping container attached to cartservice's netns at 12:20:04 with eth0 delay=300ms [tr_1a6b4ecd47ad] — is outside this system's permitted actions. If a human detaches it, confirmation would be cartservice log step gaps returning from ~0.9s to milliseconds [tr_eb7e3f4ea605] and checkoutservice error ratio falling from ~15.7% toward the ~0.13% baseline [tr_091795de4d3f].
proposal.if_wrong: Wrong if recreating cartservice via revert_config would itself drop the foreign shaping sidecar — unestablished here — or if a latency query showed p95 stepping ~300ms exactly at 12:20:04, raising confidence above medium. Reinforced by checkoutservice's unexplained 12:02:30 change point, 18 minutes before the attach [tr_091795de4d3f, tr_1a6b4ecd47ad].
proposal.risk: Abstaining leaves the 300ms delay in force and checkout shedding orders until a human intervenes. But revert_config would restore a prior recorded config, and the outstanding pair in history is REDIS_ADDR at redis-cart:6380 [tr_1a6b4ecd47ad] — reinstating it could turn latency degradation into total cart failure. restart_service fails its precondition (evidence names a change, not process state; logs show a live non-restarting process). rollback_image fails too: the hotfix image was already reverted 14 minutes before onset.
proposal.blast_radius: No one, since nothing is done. The rejected revert_config on cartservice would have reset its container: checkoutservice and frontend see connection resets on cart calls, loadgenerator records the failures, and redis-cart could see traffic move ports.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerted simultaneously along the cart/checkout/frontend path, which is more than a lone warning latency blip and cannot be dismissed. No open incident covers it and the alerts don't point to a specific mechanism yet.
